source: private authoritative inventory snapshot; identifiers and requirements preserved

criteria.requirement: All 27 required leaf issues below have their specified evidence and producer/consumer review.
Release gate #3 passes every criterion with pinned revisions and actual offline contract results.
Required interfaces are consumable by the eight requested repositories and the application composition root; no missing consumer, schema, fixture or authority agreement is hidden in an umbrella.
Every required catalog contract has an authoritative domain owner, demonstrated producer/consumer, canonical schema, canonical/generated types, validation helper and explicit version policy.
All schemas and references compile; generation is deterministic; a clean checkout reproduces the distributed package.
Each contract has positive and negative fixtures with expected codes; malformed input, required fields, stale approvals, version mismatch, unknown enums and cross-tenant misuse are covered.
Compatibility, deprecation, field stability, unknown-value and pinned-revision migration policies have producer and consumer review.
Generated type usage, validators, catalog navigation, private evidence rules and offline consumer CI instructions are documented.
Eight downstream repositories have a compatibility/pin handoff record with immutable component revisions, command outputs and reviewer acknowledgement; domain implementation remains owned downstream.

Every leaf in #1 has closure evidence; the contract test execution passes with pre-provisioned locked dependencies and exact consumer checkouts, offline and without provider credentials or financial side effects. Any blocked handoff keeps this gate open.

The getticketstub.com application composition root provides producer/consumer compatibility review and immutable pin evidence for ProjectRequest, ApprovalReference/ApprovalReceipt authority, OrderAuthorization, artifacts, quotes and status. A known application boundary cannot be omitted because it is outside this run's write scope.

For every contract record schema path/version, source-of-truth owner, producer, consumers, trust boundary, lifecycle, semantic authority, field steward and leaf issue; no missing contract is hidden in this inventory issue.

Reconcile ArtifactHandoffManifest (creative artwork to print-production) versus ProductionBundle (print output to app/fulfillment); ApprovalReference/Receipt versus OrderAuthorization (art approval versus purchase).
Record live consumer local definitions and source SHAs; flag divergent names/versions and concrete migration owners; preserve ARC-02 ownership and CON-01.
Maintain requirement -> owner issue -> dependencies -> executable verification -> closure-evidence map, including every SC-01 through SC-12 requirement; no invented consumer or global ID.

Provide schemas/, generated/, fixtures/, compatibility/ and an explicit package export map; validate schema references/formats and generation completeness. Runtime/type parity is checked using valid and invalid payloads. SC-02 establishes fixture directory/package plumbing and per-contract command hooks only; SC-09 owns canonical fixture manifests, cross-contract coverage and consumer CI behavior.

Establish npm scripts: generate, contracts:check (supports --contract), contracts:fixtures (supports --contract), contracts:compat, contracts:inventory (supports --require-owner, --require-consumer, --require-leaf, --require-version-policy, --require-field-classification, --policy-only, --require-fixtures, --require-docs and --require-consumer-pins), contracts:consumers and docs:check; generation must be deterministic and leave a clean diff. Implement every command and flag referenced by leaf validation steps; scripts consume local files/checkouts and never fetch implicitly.

Lock Node/tool versions compatible with live consumers; publish no runtime dependency on harness, creative or research repositories. Shared interfaces stay below their injected ports in the dependency graph.

Export no-network runtime validation and semantic context-check interfaces; no coercion/default insertion that silently changes signed/hash-bound values. Compile supported versions together and reject unsupported major versions with typed errors.
Define package contents, schema IDs, schema_version convention, error return shape and type declaration usage; expose an offline clean-checkout test entry point.

Treat required-field additions, semantic/unit changes, narrowing, removals and unsafe enum additions as breaking unless demonstrated compatible; define handling of unknown additive metadata separately from execution-critical controls.

Document deprecation notice, replacement, affected consumers, minimum supported window and removal condition. Support current and previous accepted major during migration; no removal until all named v1 consumers have acknowledged and passed migration fixtures.
Require producer and consumer review plus compatibility impact record before a breaking integration; test current producer/old consumer and old producer/current consumer with supported versions.

Use immutable shared-contracts SHA or integrity-locked package and record exact schema, toolchain and consumer pins. main/latest is not integration evidence; define coordinated upgrade, rollback and failed-consumer blocking behavior. Preserve CON-01/ARC-01/EVAL-01.

For every ID specify assigning authority, caller-supplied versus server-assigned status, scope, immutability, uniqueness domain, retry/redelivery behavior and when omission/unknown is valid. Tenant/project scope is authenticated context; an ID or correlation link never grants authorization.

Define producer/build revision, schema/policy revision, UTC occurred/observed/ingested times, source_refs and provenance references; distinguish event delivery identity from usage and provider attempts.

Supply context-check helpers/fixtures that reject mismatched expected tenant/project/design scope without claiming schemas perform authentication. Reject forged scope in downstream integration fixtures under CON-02.
Prove IDs survive a research -> creative -> production -> usage/evidence trace; missing provider IDs remain explicitly unavailable, never fabricated. Cover CON-02, AGT-01, FIN-01/02/03 and EVAL-01.

Classify identifiers, source URLs/text, prompts, asset locations, approval actors, provider request IDs, destinations and diagnostics; deny credentials, auth headers, signed URLs/query tokens and raw private/customer content in public evidence.

Define allowlisted public projections with synthetic/sanitized fixture inputs; strip diagnostics and metadata recursively, including unknown/additive fields. A provenance reference must not grant access or reveal sensitive storage locations.

Specify deterministic hash algorithm, canonical serialization, Unicode/numeric/time rules and byte-hash versus manifest-hash scope. Hashes bind exact artifact content; low-entropy sensitive values must not be exposed through plain stable hashes. Document tenant-scoped keyed pseudonyms where correlation is necessary and key management remains downstream.

Provide executable positive and negative EvidenceProjection fixtures. SC-09 #29 performs the comprehensive per-contract field-classification completeness audit; keep it outside this issue's closure. Preserve CON-02 and EVAL-04 without claiming public-evidence sanitization proves runtime access control.

Include stable code/category, module/operation, safe message, trace/diagnostic reference, validation paths, retryability hint, blocking condition and schema version; details must be privacy classified.

Distinguish malformed/unsupported versions or enum values, scope mismatch, stale approval, unsupported case, cancellation, timeout, rate limit, partial failure and unknown side effects/usage. Never equate timeout with confirmed failure.
Batch envelopes retain successful item identities and explicit failures; define all-or-nothing versus partial acceptance policy reference and invalid/missing/duplicate item handling.
Retryability cannot authorize spending, reissue a side effect or bypass attempts/budget/approval. Provide deterministic code registry and migration policy; preserve CON-03, AGT-03 and FIN-04.

Specify state vocabulary and legal transition/version rules for queued/running/waiting-for-review/blocked/cancel-requested/cancelled/succeeded/failed plus partial/unknown outcome. Preserve task-specific codes and total/progress unknown semantics.

Cancellation request is distinct from acknowledged terminal cancellation; after-dispatch cancellation may leave provider side effects or unknown usage. Include request ID, idempotency key, sequence/revision, time, resume/checkpoint reference, and typed rejection.

Define duplicate/out-of-order/stale progress handling, terminal result references, partial completion, ownership/lease attempt correlation and safe error links. A contract describes transitions; harness implements execution/recovery.

Fixtures include stale sequence, wrong scope, invalid transition, duplicate command, resume after terminal status and cancellation while a provider attempt remains uncertain. Link global AGT-02/03 and FIN-04.

Distinguish one logical operation, each provider execution, transport retry, separately billed attempt and duplicate observation. Provider adapters declare whether a retry reuses provider/idempotency identity or starts a new potentially billable attempt.

Represent usage completeness and valuation separately: unknown/incomplete/complete observations; unknown/estimated/provider-confirmed valuation; never encode unknown as zero. Include units, model/provider, currency/precision, rate-card and policy versions, environment/billing mode, outcome and provider ID when available.

Define duplicate/redelivery/correction identity, linked superseding observations and reconciliation references without implementing deduplication or posting. Estimated and confirmed observations must be joinable without another charge.

Fixtures: two billed attempts under one logical operation remain distinct; duplicate observation is the same observation; transport retry may retain execution identity; timeout with unknown usage is retained; observed zero is explicitly measured; live/sandbox/simulated do not collapse. Preserve FIN-01/02/03/04/05/07 and BUD-03.

Carry reservation identity, trusted scope, logical/billed attempt, policy version, currency/exact amounts, held/consumed values, lifecycle and expiry, idempotency/correlation and authoritative issuer/result references.
Distinguish granted/denied/unknown/unavailable, consumed/released/expired and uncertain in-flight states; timeout or cancellation cannot justify releasing a hold when execution may still occur.

Define settlement evidence, expiry eligibility and retry reconciliation requirements without allowing caller claims to mint budget authority. Unknown usage preserves uncertainty and finance controls the state transition.
Fixtures cover scope mismatch, negative/imprecise amounts, currency mismatch, duplicate reserve/settle observation and attempted expiry/release of uncertain work. Preserve BUD-01/02/03/04 and FIN-04.

Specify period, currency, exact decimal/scaled-integer representation, scale/rounding boundary, metric definitions, original amounts, policy/rate-card references and source coverage; retain sub-cent precision.

Separate estimate/confirmed valuation, payment settlement, reconciliation, reservation lifecycle and reporting completeness; absent/unknown totals are not zero and currencies are not silently combined.

Identify included environments and billing modes, project/tenant scope and provenance/revision so totals can be reproduced by the finance owner. Refer to refund/credit/reversal/payment sources without defining new financial authority.

Fixtures cover sub-cent aggregation representation, multiple currencies, partial/unknown coverage and isolated simulated/live summaries. Preserve FIN-05/07/08/10; domain arithmetic proof stays in cost-intelligence.

Define stable question IDs, schema/policy/model references, immutable state/evidence references, scope, eligible actions/candidates, deadline/cancellation, budget/attempt references and bounded batch size. Independent questions may batch; dependent questions require staged input with no sibling-answer reads.

Define Choice selected value and probability map/confidence, Score numeric result/legend/probabilities/confidence, and Noul numeric probability (no invented confidence field). Specify numeric bounds, distributions/tolerance, missing/extra questions and invalid values; no result expands the caller's allowlist.

Resolve the real Score criteria/legend conflict with harness, EI and creative owners: EI v1 requires strings, creative uses array/object forms, harness wire accepts structured forms. Pin the discrepancy decision and lossless adapter or versioned migration with fixtures; do not silently normalize it.

Represent unknown, abstain, low-confidence/review, unavailable, timeout, cancelled and malformed responses; partial batch and all-or-nothing behavior must be explicit. Timeout never asserts no provider charge or authorizes an automatic paid retry.

DecisionReceipt binds request, question/answer/batch IDs and hashes, schema/policy/model revisions, normalized result, decision time, trace/evidence and usage/attempt references, and review reason. It is evidence of a decision, never approval/purchase authority.

Fixture suite covers all result variants including Noul-with-confidence rejection, stale policy, invalid distributions, cyclic/dependent questions, extra capabilities, unknown enum, partial batch and timeout. Preserve CON-03 and AGT-03/04.
Separate untrusted submitted URL/customer content from trusted server scope; caller-supplied tenant/project/permission fields cannot override expected authenticated context.
Specify required inputs, supported output types and limits, optional values, schema_version/contract discriminator and safe source references; unsupported actions/types produce SC-08 errors.

Fixtures include minimal/full valid requests, missing fields, wrong tenant/project, unknown output/action, malformed URLs and old-version/additive-field behavior. URL fetch/SSRF execution and identity authentication remain app/harness responsibilities.
Record producer/consumer reviewer agreement and migration from harness's local public runtime request types; preserve CON-02/03 and AGT-05.
Publish a separately identifiable ResearchRequest export and fixture set; ProjectRequest is not a substitute and raw user content cannot grant tools, domains, budget or permission.

Define required/optional fields, idempotency and request/schema/policy IDs, deadline/cancel references, result expectation and unsupported-case errors. No request embeds harness implementation objects or provider auth.

Fixtures cover missing source/input, mismatched scope, forged capability/budget overrides, stale policy/version and valid minimal/full requests; trusted callbacks/context remain application/harness responsibilities.
Record explicit handoff review with event-intelligence and harness using exact shared-contracts SHA; retain local proposal adapters until accepted. Preserve CON-01/02/03.

Represent fact value/unknown/conflicting/review states and confidence basis without erasing source disagreements. Separate event facts from creative interpretation and public discovery from reproduction permission.

Define asset candidates versus permission-bound approved asset references, original/transformed hashes, intended use and source retention/access constraints. Artifacts require an external approval reference; a discovered URL is not permission.

Resolve EventIntelligencePackage versus ResearchPackage alias and creative's proposed v1.0/v1.1 compatibility. Define canonical names and lossless adapters; review exact field changes and additive behavior with the EI producer and creative consumer.

Include request/answer/batch receipt references, schema/policy versions and independent package identity (event_id is delivery identity). Fixtures cover missing provenance, contradictory facts, stale assets, unknown facts, alias drift and wrong scope. Preserve AGT-01, ART-05 and CON-01/02.

Bind correction to expected package version/hash, actor/authority reference and trusted scope; represent proposed versus accepted correction, source provenance and new immutable parent-linked package. No in-place mutation or caller boolean approval.

Invalidations identify event/source observation, affected package/asset versions, reason (freshness/rights/correction), effective time, monotonic revision and scope; define duplicate/out-of-order/stale behavior.

Define acknowledgements and receipt/evidence references while durable delivery/CAS/recomputation remain downstream. Invalidation marks affected approval/use stale and does not silently rewrite a DesignVersion.

Fixtures cover forged scope, stale expected version, duplicate and out-of-order invalidation, revoked asset rights and valid parent chain; migrate current EI local correction/cache event APIs with consumer review. Preserve AGT-01, ART-02/05 and CON-02.

Bind brief identity/version/hash to exact research package/fact/asset versions and provenance. Preserve uncertainty/review blocking; unsupported or unapproved asset references cannot become implicit approval.

Carry product/output constraints, model policy/schema versions and tenant/project scope without model credentials or executable instructions/capabilities. Separate composition facts from generated image prompts.
Fixtures cover sourced valid brief, unknown/conflicting facts, stale/revoked asset refs, missing constraints, mixed-tenant evidence and unsupported policy. Preserve AGT-01, ART-05 and CON-02/03.
Review/migrate current creative local brief validators and EI handoff with explicit old-version fixtures and pinned producer/consumer revisions.
Reject executable UI code, scripts, arbitrary actions, privileged capability declarations and unknown execution-critical controls. Labels/descriptions are inert text.
Specify required/optional/default behavior, field stability, numeric units/ranges and enum evolution; controls bind an immutable supported design/policy version and trusted scope.
Fixtures cover safe controls, range violations, invalid default/enum, unknown control/action, script-bearing field and stale schema version. Preserve CON-03.
Document migration of creative's existing local controls while avoiding importing UI/runtime libraries into the shared package.
An edit creates a new version; parent/design/project scope must agree. No approval binds a mutable latest pointer. Specify exact byte hash and manifest/hash canonicalization rules from SC-11.
Separate original/generated/transformed artwork identity, displayed preview identity and eventual production output identity; print-production remains exact output composition owner.
Define cancelled/partial job artifact availability and immutable status references; no successful DesignVersion for missing or unverifiable artifact bytes.

Fixtures cover branch lineage, missing parent/hash, mixed design/tenant, mismatched preview/artwork and mutated content. Preserve ART-01/02 and CON-02; persistence/concurrency implementations remain creative-owned.

Bind trusted issuer/audience/actor, tenant/project, subject type and immutable design/artwork/package/asset versions/hashes, intended use, preview and composition/fact hashes where approval claims cover them, issue/expiry time and revocation/status reference.
Distinguish reference, issuer receipt, verification outcome and handoff consumption receipt. Creative's local ConsumptionReceipt is not ApprovalReceipt and boolean approved=true is never authority.

Define current authenticated verifier input and stale/expired/revoked/wrong-issuer/wrong-audience handling. Structural schema validates shape; the application verifies authenticity/current authorization and supplies trusted context.

Any approved subject mutation or transformed artifact requires revalidation/new approval as appropriate; bind the exact displayed immutable artifact. No mutable URL/latest pointer alone satisfies approval.

Fixtures include valid external receipt and forged issuer, wrong tenant/project/hash/version/use, expiry/revocation, changed facts/composition and transformed-byte reuse. Preserve ART-02/05 and CON-02.

Include manifest identity/version/hash, tenant/project/design/version, exact artwork bytes/hash/media metadata, approved preview identity, external ApprovalReference, fact/asset permission references, requested product/print constraints and provenance/usage/decision references.

Represent artifact locator/access policy separately from stable identity and bytes hash; signed URLs/auth tokens/private storage paths cannot appear in public evidence. Define access expiry versus artifact immutability.

Validate agreement among manifest, approved immutable design/artwork and intended production use; stale/revoked approval or mismatched hashes blocks handoff. Do not claim artwork handoff is a finished print-ready bundle.

Define idempotent handoff/consumption receipt reference and migration from creative's local manifest/ConsumptionReceipt names. Fixtures cover mutated artwork, latest aliases, expired locator, wrong scope and duplicate handoff. Preserve ART-02/04/05.

Carry bundle ID/version/hash, design/artifact approval refs, renderer/template/font versions, exact composed fact/barcode inputs, product/spec identity, file names/media/dimensions/units/hashes and preflight report/result references.

Specify deterministic manifest hashing and complete file set; separate source-artwork hash, displayed-preview hash and final print-output hash. Final composition changes cannot reuse an unrelated approval or authorization claim.
Represent preflight passed/failed/unsupported/unknown with typed blocking reasons; bundle presence alone is not evidence of successful rendering/preflight.
Fixtures cover valid manifest, missing output, altered file hash, wrong print units/spec, absent/failed preflight and stale approval. Preserve ART-04 and CON-01/02.

Include provider/quote identity, product/variant, quantity, destination reference, shipping method, currency/exact charge breakdown, issued/expiry time, applicability to specification/bundle revision, source observation and environment/billing mode.
Distinguish quoted/estimated/unknown charges and quote validity from authorization/payment/settlement. Never leak customer shipping details into public fixtures/evidence.
Define changed-terms, expired-quote, unsupported product/destination and partial supplier data errors; amount/precision policy matches shared primitives.
Fixtures cover expiry, currency mismatch, charge total representation, changed quantity/destination/bundle/spec and unknown fields/enums. Preserve FUL-01/02 and FIN-07.

Bind issuer/actor/tenant/project/order, quote identity, maximum exact amount/currency, product/quantity, destination/shipping reference, exact ProductionBundle hash, issue/expiry/revocation and idempotency references.
Changed purchase terms require renewed authorization, including quantity, destination, bundle, currency or maximum amount. A retryability hint, budget hold, quote or art approval cannot substitute.
Define trusted verification context and stale/forged/mismatch/expired errors, without implementing authentication, signing secrets, purchasing or supplier submission.
Fixtures cover valid authorization and every changed-term case, cross-tenant order, forged issuer, expired/revoked receipt and duplicate submission reference; preserve FUL-01/02/03 and CON-02.

Specify provider/supplier-order identity, internal order/bundle/authorization reference, source observation identity/time, normalized status and opaque provider status, last-known state and uncertainty.

Distinguish submission timeout with unknown outcome from rejected/accepted/cancelled/fulfilled. Cancellation requested differs from supplier-confirmed cancellation; no contract permits automatic new purchase on timeout.

Define duplicate/out-of-order callback semantics and stable external idempotency reference; repeated observation is not new order/charge, while a truly distinct provider execution retains a distinct attempt.
Fixtures cover duplicate callback, delayed state regression, ambiguous submission, unknown provider enum, cross-tenant identity and rejected cancellation. Preserve FUL-03/04 and FIN-02/03/04.

Include evidence/run/scenario IDs, unchanged acceptance IDs, exact component/contract/tool revisions, input identity/hash, fixture identity, provider/dependency mode, timestamps, commands, results, metrics/units and comparison/baseline basis.

Distinguish planned, passed, failed, blocked and unmeasured assertions with explicit limitations; store actual evidence artifact hashes/locators and related decision/usage/trace IDs. Unknown measurement is not zero/pass.

Use public-evidence projection from SC-11 and private-access references; prohibit credentials, raw prompts/source/customer details and signed artifact URLs. Versioned input/result hashes must be reproducible.

Fixtures cover missing revision, mismatched input/hash, stale schema, ambiguous mode, forged acceptance claim and sensitive nested fields. Preserve EVAL-01/04, CON-02 and ARC-01; global status changes remain integration-evals work.

Inventory every required contract/version with valid minimal/full and invalid malformed JSON, missing required fields, wrong types, unknown enums, unsupported major and supported older-version/additive-field cases. Missing fixture/schema/validator/generated export fails CI.

Include stale/forged approval and altered hash, wrong tenant/project/artifact identity, duplicate versus separately billed attempts, unknown usage, out-of-order progress/invalidation and partial DecisionPort batches. Expected typed code/path and policy version are data in the fixture manifest.

Round-trip canonical fixtures through generated producer/consumer bindings and compare bytes/hashes where bound; check runtime/type parity, serialization drift and immutable pin compatibility. Prove rejection assertions themselves fail if the validator incorrectly accepts a negative fixture.

Provide npm run contracts:consumers using a checked-in exact-revision manifest plus pre-provisioned local checkout/artifact paths at the exact SHAs; never clone or fetch implicitly. Cover harness, research, creative, production, fulfillment, finance, dashboard and integration-evals, and the `getticketstub.com` composition root as a mandatory producer/consumer compatibility-review and pin-handoff target. Exercise its `ProjectRequest` and `OrderAuthorization` producer/consumer roles, approval issuer/binding, and `FulfillmentQuote` and normalized fulfillment-status producer/consumer roles; record the composition-root exact SHA in the manifest and evidence. A missing exact-SHA checkout or consumer integration is blocked, never skipped/pass; make no network/provider calls.

Document copy/import package fixture consumption and exact downstream CI command; execute scope-sensitive integration cases in trusted consumer adapters, not JSON Schema alone. Schemas do not prove authorization, budget atomicity, durable recovery or ledger arithmetic.
Output sanitized machine-readable and human-readable coverage/evidence keyed by unchanged global IDs and local SC namespaces. Preserve CON-01/02/03, ART-02/04/05, FIN-02/03/04 and EVAL-01/04.

README links every catalog contract to schema, generated types, helper, fixture examples and owner; docs include copyable supported Node ESM/TypeScript usage, version negotiation, safe errors and context validation examples.

Document migration from consumer-local definitions, current compatibility disagreements and immutable pin upgrades/rollback. Shared catalog is canonical; architecture snapshot links remain historical context rather than a competing source.

Provide a per-consumer handoff matrix for all eight downstream repos and the `getticketstub.com` composition root. Include the composition root's `ProjectRequest` and `OrderAuthorization` producer/consumer roles, approval issuer and binding, and `FulfillmentQuote` and normalized fulfillment-status producer/consumer roles. Each row records accountable role, accepted schema/package/source SHA, tested consumer or composition-root SHA, fixture digest, exact command, result/limitations and acknowledgement; unavailable integrations keep release blocked.

Define package content/export map and reproducible archive, registry/tag/version mapping, changelog/deprecation notes and release evidence checklist. Review artifact privacy, dependency provenance and asset rights; do not invent a license or publish automatically.

Reconcile stale public/private wording in ownership documentation against inspected repository metadata without changing visibility. Keep documentation and acceptance status honest; preserve ARC-01 and EVAL-01/04.
